title: Deduplication does not increase clause length
statement: Let $c$ be a clause, that is, a finite list of literals over the variables $\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$, and let $\mathrm{dedup}(c)$ be the clause obtained from $c$ by retaining, for each variable, only its first occurring literal and discarding every later literal on the same variable. Then the length of $\mathrm{dedup}(c)$ is at most the length of $c$.
hypotheses_covered: c is a list of literals over Fin n
replaced: The length of $\mathrm{dedupClauseVars}\,c$ is at most the length of $c$.
